## 1. Record the gate's outcome in the ledger

I record the revert before doing anything else. If the gate restarts, it will show the Task 2 ruling as reverted and ask nothing about it.

<edit path=".sdd/12-dock-alerts/progress.md">
Reverted at the gate: Task 2 ruling — alert at 3 or fewer free slots, not 2 or fewer
Gate: partner ruled email is fine for alerts at night — no change, nothing deferred.
Follow-up 1: revert Task 2 threshold to 2 or fewer free slots (spec § 2) — in progress
</edit>

## 2. Implement the revert now (protocol step 1)

The revert is a follow-up task, so I dispatch one implementer subagent with this brief:

> Follow-up task for plan `specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md` on `feat/dock-alerts`. The Task 2 commits (8c9d0e1..a4b5c6d) set the alert threshold to "3 or fewer free slots." Change it back to "2 or fewer free slots," as `specs/dock-alerts.md` § 2 says. Update every test that pins the threshold. A dock with 2 free slots alerts, and a dock with 3 does not. Touch nothing else. Run the full suite and commit.

When it returns, I dispatch the task reviewer on that commit range, checked against spec § 2. I fix anything it finds before I continue. Once the review is clean, I update the ledger:

<edit path=".sdd/12-dock-alerts/progress.md">
Follow-up 1: complete (commits 0b1c2d3..<new-sha>, review clean)
</edit>

## 3. Finish the protocol: markup, deferred items, retire

**Plan markup.** I mark all four tasks and the follow-up done:

<edit path="specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md">
Status: complete (2026-11-18). Tasks 1–4 done; follow-up 1 reverted the Task 2 threshold to spec § 2 (2 or fewer free slots). Task 3 module is `alerts/notify.py`, not `alerts/send.py`.
</edit>

**Deferred items.** There are none to add. The night-email question is ruled, no finding is unfixed, and nothing was skipped. `specs/deferred_items.md` stays unchanged.

**History entry.** The entry leaves out the reverted Task 2 ruling. None of the remaining rulings contradicts the spec, so no spec amendment is needed.

<edit path="specs/history.md">
## 12-dock-alerts (completed 2026-11-18)
Plan: specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md — Spec: specs/dock-alerts.md
Rulings taken:
- Task 3: module is `alerts/notify.py`, not `alerts/send.py` — `send` shadows the socket helper the service already imports.
- Task 3: alerts are not batched; one email per alert, as spec § 3 says.
- Final review: retry-jitter finding left out — the tests seed the jitter on purpose.
Gate: email confirmed as the channel for alerts at night.
</edit>

**Retire the plan:**

<command>git mv specs/plans/12-dock-alerts.md specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md</command>
<command>git add specs/history.md specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md && git commit -m "Complete plan 12-dock-alerts"</command>

## 4. Delete the workspace

This runs last, after the protocol and with the follow-up merged on the branch. I delete it by its literal path and leave sibling directories alone:

<command>rm -rf .sdd/12-dock-alerts</command>

---

**Message to my partner:**

> Done as you ruled:
> - **Task 2 reverted.** A follow-up task set the threshold back to 2 or fewer free slots (spec § 2), with tests pinning both 2 (alerts) and 3 (doesn't). It passed review and is on `feat/dock-alerts`.
> - **Other rulings stand.** They are recorded in `specs/history.md`: the `alerts/notify.py` module name, one email per alert, and the jitter finding left out.
> - **Night alerts stay on email.** Nothing was deferred, so `specs/deferred_items.md` is unchanged.
>
> The plan is now at `specs/plans/completed/12-dock-alerts.md` and the `.sdd/12-dock-alerts` workspace is deleted. The branch is ready for finishing-a-development-branch.
